frsc-towing-sop-2019.documentReference: 8-page PDF signed 22 October 2019; Scope & Limitations pp. 3–4; Towing on Request & Broken-down Vehicles p. 5; Mode of Payment & Release p. 6; Recommended Tow Charges table p. 7; Towing Requisition Form p. 8
frsc-towing-sop-2019.notes: Publicly linked from https://frsc.gov.ng/documentations/standard-operating-procedures (HTTP 200 on 31 October 2026). Paragraph 15 (p. 7) states that FRSC tow charges are the average of prevailing commercial charges subject to distance, tonnage, terrain and PMS/AGO price regime, and publishes a recommended guide ranging from ₦5,000 to ₦95,000 across 6 distance/time bands and 4 vehicle/terrain columns. Paragraph 10(c) (p. 5) states that a broken-down vehicle undergoing long repairs with the owner in sight is towed off the road to a safe place at no cost. The April 2026 SLA (Printed p. 17; PDF p. 17) retains the variable commercial-average formula and daily custody fee after 20 hours (Printed p. 14; PDF p. 14) without reprinting the 2019 numeric table.

services.name: Driver's licence — motor vehicle (other classes, 3 years)
services.jurisdiction: Federal baseline (with State IRS / VIO / MVAA steps)
services.description: Three-year National Driver's Licence for motor vehicles (Private, Commercial/Professional and other non-Class A categories), covering fresh applications, renewals and re-issues.
requirements: Minimum age of 18 years for a Private Driver's Licence, or 26 years with an existing Private Driver's Licence for a Commercial/Professional Driver's Licence.

For fresh applicants: valid Learner's Permit issued by State BIR/MVAA, DSSP completion certificate code (26 sessions + CBT with at least 60% score, valid for 6 months) from an FRSC-accredited driving school, and VIO Driver's Test Certificate.
For renewals: existing National Driver's Licence (renewable within 1 calendar month before expiration; SLA p. 7 states a VIO retest applies if 6 months have elapsed since holding a valid licence).
For lost or damaged replacement: police extract and court sworn affidavit as required on the NDL portal.
Vision Acuity Test at the FRSC Driver's Licence Centre (DLC) and in-person biometric capture (unless eligible for odd-renewal Bypass Capture).
processSteps: Fresh applicants first obtain a Learner's Permit from the State BIR/MVAA, complete 26 training sessions and CBT at an accredited driving school (https://dssp.frsc.gov.ng/), and pass the VIO proficiency test.
Complete the National Driver's Licence application or renewal form online on https://nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng/.
Pay the prescribed ₦15,000 fee online or at a designated bank/payment channel and have payment confirmed by the State Board of Internal Revenue (BIR) / MVAA.

Attend the FRSC Driver's Licence Centre (DLC) in person for Vision Acuity Test and biometric capture (fingerprints, facial photo and signature) to receive a Temporary Driver's Licence valid for 60 days (odd renewals 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th may use Bypass Capture online).
Collect the permanent National Driver's Licence in person from the State IRS / MVAA office after FRSC production (service standard: 60 days from temporary card issuance at the DLC).
services.notes: Multi-authority governance (FRSC / VIO / State IRS & JTB): FRSC designs and produces the National Driver's Licence and Number Plates and captures biometrics at Driver's Licence Centres (DLCs); State Vehicle Inspection Officers (VIO) conduct driver proficiency testing; State Boards of Internal Revenue (SBIR / FCT-IRS) and Motor Licensing Authorities (MLA / MVAA) determine state collectible charges through the Joint Tax Board (JTB), confirm payments and distribute permanent cards/plates. Service standard timeline: 60 days from issuance of the Temporary Driver's Licence at the FRSC DLC.
services.paymentGuide: Apply through the official Nigeria Driver's Licence portal (https://nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng/) and pay through the approved portal/bank channel. Keep State BIR learner permit, driving school, VIO test and bank charges separate from the ₦15,000 licence fee.

services.jurisdiction: Federal baseline (with Government Hospital, VIO & State IRS steps)
services.description: Issuance of a Commercial or Professional National Driver's Licence for drivers employed by registered transport companies or belonging to recognised transport associations.
requirements: Applicant must NOT be below 26 years of age and must already possess a valid Private Driver's Licence.
Evidence of membership of a professional transport association (such as NURTW or NARTO) or letter of employment from a registered transport company.

Medical Certificate of Fitness from a designated Government Hospital covering: (1) Blood pressure/hypertension, (2) Visual acuity & colour blindness, (3) Blood sugar, (4) Arthritis, (5) Electroencephalogram (EEG) screening for epilepsy, and (6) Ear examination.
Pass the VIO driving proficiency test and obtain a Driver's Test Certificate (unsuccessful applicants wait 1 calendar month before re-examination).
Vision Acuity Test and in-person biometric capture at an FRSC Driver's Licence Centre (DLC).
processSteps: Obtain the required Medical Certificate of Fitness from a designated Government Hospital and evidence of NURTW/NARTO membership or company employment.
Undergo the driving proficiency test with the State Vehicle Inspection Officer (VIO) and obtain the Driver's Test Certificate.

Complete the application on https://nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng/, pay the prescribed licence fee (₦15,000 for 3 years or ₦21,000 for 5 years for motor vehicles; ₦7,000 for 3 years or ₦11,000 for 5 years for motorcycles/tricycles), and confirm payment at State BIR/MVAA.
Present documents and complete Vision Acuity Test and biometric capture at the FRSC DLC to receive a 60-day Temporary Driver's Licence.
Collect the permanent Commercial/Professional Driver's Licence at the State IRS/MVAA after 60 days.

services.name: Foreign Driver's Licence Reciprocity (conversion to Nigerian Driver's Licence)
services.jurisdiction: Federal (FRSC DLC, RSHQ Abuja Foreign Desk, VIO & State BIR)
services.description: Conversion of a valid foreign driver's licence into a Nigerian National Driver's Licence through FRSC reciprocity verification and VIO re-testing, bypassing the 26-session driving school training.
requirements: Data page of International Passport.
Valid Foreign Driver's Licence.
Proof of residence in Nigeria.
Letter of authentication or Driving History from the country of origin / issuance of the foreign licence.
Driver's Test Certificate issued by the State VIO / Testing Officer after a proficiency re-test.
processSteps: Stage 1: Report physically to the Sector or Unit Head of the FRSC Driver's Licence Centre (DLC) with the foreign licence, passport data page, proof of residence and authentication/driving history.
Stage 2: Undergo a driving re-test conducted by the State VIO/Testing Officer to obtain a Driver's Test Certificate.
Stage 3: The DLC scans and forwards all required documents to the FRSC National Headquarters (RSHQ) Abuja Foreign Desk Officer via foreigndriverslicence@frsc.gov.ng.

Stage 4: The Reviewing Officer and Approving Officer at RSHQ review and approve the application on the DSSP portal to generate a unique identity number without the 26-session driving school requirement.

Stage 5: Complete the driver's licence form online or at the centre using the generated code, pay the applicable fee via bank/e-payment, and obtain payment confirmation from the State Board of Internal Revenue (BIR).
Stage 6: Complete in-person biometric capture at the FRSC DLC to receive a Temporary Driver's Licence while the permanent card is produced.
services.notes: SLA Printed pp. 9–10; PDF pp. 9–10. Neither the April 2026 SLA nor current public FRSC pages state whether reciprocity applicants pay only the standard NDL class fee or an additional reciprocity verification charge. The fee therefore remains pending.
services.paymentGuide: Start in person at an FRSC Driver's Licence Centre (DLC) for document verification and VIO re-test before paying through the State BIR-confirmed portal/bank route.

feeOptions.label: Foreign driver's licence reciprocity fee
feeOptions.conditions: Requires in-person submission at an FRSC DLC, VIO re-test, RSHQ Foreign Desk approval (foreigndriverslicence@frsc.gov.ng) and State BIR payment confirmation.
feeOptions.notes: Missing price in the SLA is recorded as pending/unknown, not free.
feeOptions.page: SLA Printed pp. 9–10, PDF pp. 9–10
feeOptions.evidenceNote: SLA Stage 5 (p. 10) states that the applicant makes payment through the bank/e-payment platform confirmed by the State Board of Internal Revenue, but does not state a specific reciprocity fee amount. No public FRSC schedule independently establishes the total reciprocity fee.

services.name: National Driver's Licence Online Verification & Driving Record Extract
services.jurisdiction: Federal (FRSC National Headquarters / Online Verification Portal)
services.description: Official FRSC verification of a Nigerian National Driver's Licence and issuance of an official verification report/driving record extract addressed to an established organisation (embassy, foreign licensing authority, government body, private company or NGO).
requirements: Account registration on https://ndlverification.frsc.gov.ng/ with valid contact details.
Signed formal Application Letter.
Clear front and back scan/upload of the Nigerian National Driver's Licence.
Valid means of identification (Voter's Card, International Passport or NIN).
Full official receiver address of an established organisation (Private, Government or NGO). Personal or residential delivery addresses are not accepted.
processSteps: Sign up or log in at https://ndlverification.frsc.gov.ng/ and verify your account via the emailed link.
Complete the verification request form, providing the receiving organisation's address (not a personal address).
Upload the signed application letter, front and back of the driver's licence, and valid ID.
Pay the applicable verification and/or shipping fee online via Remita using a debit card and retain the confirmation receipt.

Track processing on the portal: the public portal FAQ states 3–10 working days for in-house verification plus shipping. Under SLA Item 28 (pp. 26–27), a 10-working-day service standard and Default Approval procedure apply to complete, unflagged requests.
services.notes: Public portal: https://ndlverification.frsc.gov.ng/ and /faqs. SLA Printed pp. 10–11, 26–27; PDF pp. 10–11, 26–27. Default Approval applies ONLY to driver's record verification requests not decided or queried within 10 working days from receipt of a complete, paid application, excluding: (a) flagged records under investigation, (b) unsigned application, (c) irregular/cut-and-paste signature, (d) wrong licence uploaded, (e) no agency receiver address, (f) security/sensitive cases, and (g) face mismatch.
services.paymentGuide: Apply only on https://ndlverification.frsc.gov.ng/. Because the ₦50,000 figure appears only in the confidential SLA copy (p. 11) and is not published on the public portal FAQ, confirm the exact Remita verification/shipping charge displayed inside the official portal before paying.

feeOptions.label: Driver's licence verification and/or shipping charge
feeOptions.conditions: Processed verification documents are addressed only to established organisations (Private, Government or NGO), never to personal addresses. Standard timeline: 10 working days (3–10 working days in-house verification on portal FAQ).
feeOptions.notes: Marked pending under the FeeLens confidentiality and public-evidence rule because the ₦50,000 SLA figure lacks independent non-confidential public substantiation.
feeOptions.page: Public portal FAQ (https://ndlverification.frsc.gov.ng/faqs); SLA Printed pp. 10–11, 26–27, PDF pp. 10–11, 26–27
feeOptions.evidenceNote: The live public portal FAQ states: "You will be required to make payment for verification or shipping fee or both using the debit card" without publishing a numeric price. The supplied April 2026 SLA (marked -CONFIDENTIAL-, p. 11) mentions "payment of N50,000 for verification or shipping through REMITA", which is not independently substantiated on any non-confidential public FRSC page.

services.name: Driver and Rider Certification from Accredited Driving Schools (DSSP)
services.description: Mandatory pre-licensing training, physical capture and Computer Based Test (CBT) at an FRSC-accredited driving school under the Driving School Standardization Programme (DSSP) for fresh motor vehicle drivers (26 sessions) and motorcycle/tricycle riders (8 sessions).
requirements: Registration with an FRSC-accredited driving school listed on https://dssp.frsc.gov.ng/.
Valid Learner's Permit obtained from the State Board of Internal Revenue (BIR) / Motor Licensing Authority.

For Motor Vehicle Driver Certification (SLA pp. 23–24): completion of 25 theoretical and practical training sessions of at least 1 hour each, followed by physical capture and CBT on the 26th session (minimum pass mark: 60%; 7-day wait to rewrite if below 60%).

For Motorcycle/Tricycle Rider Certification (SLA pp. 24–25): completion of 7 theoretical and practical training sessions of at least 1 hour each, followed by physical capture and CBT on the 8th session (minimum pass mark: 60%; 7-day wait to rewrite if below 60%).
processSteps: Visit https://dssp.frsc.gov.ng/ to choose a certified driving school and enrol.
Obtain a Learner's Permit from the State Board of Internal Revenue (BIR) / MVAA so the driving school can log your permit number on the DSSP portal.
Complete the mandatory training sessions (25 sessions for motor vehicle drivers; 7 sessions for motorcycle/tricycle riders) of at least 1 hour per session.
Attend the final session (26th session for drivers; 8th session for riders) for physical capture and the Computer Based Test (CBT); score at least 60% to pass (or wait 7 days to re-sit).
Receive the DSSP Driving/Rider Certificate code (valid for 6 months) and proceed to https://nigeriadriverslicence.frsc.gov.ng/ and the VIO driving test.
services.notes: SLA Printed pp. 23–25; PDF pp. 23–25; Public DSSP portal: https://dssp.frsc.gov.ng/. The DSSP certificate is valid for 6 months from issuance.
services.paymentGuide: Select an accredited driving school on https://dssp.frsc.gov.ng/. Learner's Permit fees are paid to your State BIR/MVAA, and training tuition is paid to the accredited driving school.

feeOptions.label: Motor vehicle driver DSSP training (26 sessions + CBT) & State BIR Learner's Permit
feeOptions.conditions: 25 training sessions (minimum 1 hour each) + 26th session physical capture and CBT (60% pass mark; 6-month certificate validity). Tuition varies by accredited driving school; Learner's Permit fee is set by the relevant State BIR/MVAA.
feeOptions.notes: Separate from the ₦15,000 / ₦21,000 National Driver's Licence fee.
feeOptions.page: Public DSSP portal; SLA Printed pp. 23–24, PDF pp. 23–24
feeOptions.evidenceNote: Official FRSC sources confirm mandatory enrolment at an accredited driving school and a State BIR Learner's Permit, but neither the SLA nor the public DSSP portal fixes a uniform national tuition or Learner's Permit tariff.

feeOptions.label: Motorcycle / tricycle rider DSSP training (8 sessions + CBT) & State BIR Learner's Permit
feeOptions.conditions: 7 training sessions (minimum 1 hour each) + 8th session physical capture and CBT (60% pass mark; 6-month certificate validity). Tuition varies by accredited driving school; Learner's Permit fee is set by State BIR/MVAA.
feeOptions.notes: Separate from the ₦7,000 / ₦11,000 Class A Rider's Licence fee.
feeOptions.page: Public DSSP portal; SLA Printed pp. 24–25, PDF pp. 24–25
feeOptions.evidenceNote: The SLA (pp. 24–25) specifies 7 training sessions + 8th session physical capture and CBT for riders, with Learner's Permit issued by State BIR and tuition set by the accredited driving school.

services.name: Driving School Registration, Certification and Branch Accreditation (DSSP)
services.description: Registration, facility inspection, certification and annual permit renewal for corporate or individual operators establishing a main or branch driving school in Nigeria under the FRSC Driving School Standardization Programme (DSSP).
requirements: Completed application form (Form TSC0001 in the public SOP; Form TRG00001 in the April 2026 SLA) via https://dssp.frsc.gov.ng/ or the nearest FRSC Command.
CAC Certificate of Incorporation / Business Name registration and current Tax Clearance Certificate.

Required instructional facilities and equipment: Conducive classroom, Administrative office, Functional convenience, Practice/manoeuvring range, Roadworthy learner vehicles (at least 1 vehicle per category applied for, fitted with dual brake/clutch controls, First Aid box, fire extinguisher, L-plates and school name), Highway Code, traffic-sign charts, magnetic board, workbench/car Engines & Gear system, desktop computer with internet access, driving simulator and projector.

Qualified instructors holding a valid certificate from an FRSC-accredited driving school and a valid National Driver's Licence with at least 3 years driving experience without conviction for drunken driving.
processSteps: Obtain and complete the driving school registration form on https://dssp.frsc.gov.ng/ or at the nearest FRSC Command (if opening a branch, apply as a new school with a copy of the main school's approval certificate).
FRSC Sector Command DSSP committee conducts physical inspection of the proposed school's classroom, range, vehicles, simulator, instructional aids and instructors.
Sector Commander forwards the inspection report to FRSC National Headquarters (RSHQ) Abuja within 1 week of inspection.

Following RSHQ verification and approval, FRSC issues a Certificate of Compliance (valid for 1 year and renewable annually upon re-inspection) and activates portal access on https://dssp.frsc.gov.ng/.
services.notes: Public SOP: https://staging.frsc.gov.ng/frsc-admin/uploads/sopds_e1cd918588.pdf (pp. 1–7); SLA Printed pp. 21–23, PDF pp. 21–23. Service standard in SLA: Sector Command forwards inspection report to RSHQ within 1 week; Approved Driving School Certificate is valid for 1 year and renewable annually.
services.paymentGuide: Apply through https://dssp.frsc.gov.ng/ or the nearest FRSC Sector Command. Confirm with FRSC whether a registration fee currently applies under Form TRG00001 before making payment.

feeOptions.label: Driving school registration and certification (Form TSC0001 / TRG00001)
feeOptions.conditions: Applies to main school and branch registration under DSSP. Approval certificate is valid for 1 year and subject to annual renewal and monthly re-inspection.
feeOptions.notes: Marked conflicting (with unknown amount) because the public SOP states Form TSC0001 is obtained at no cost while the 2026 SLA states a prescribed registration fee is mandatory without publishing the amount.
feeOptions.page: Public Driving School SOP p. 2 (Section 5.1); SLA Printed p. 21, PDF p. 21 (Sections B.2 & C)
feeOptions.evidenceNote: Official FRSC documents disagree on whether a fee applies: the public Driving School SOP (sopds_e1cd918588.pdf, Section 5.1, p. 2) states that prospective operators obtain Form TSC0001 from the nearest FRSC office "at no cost" or download it online, whereas the April 2026 SLA (Printed p. 21; PDF p. 21, Sections B.2 & C) states under Form TRG00001 that "no driving school shall be registered unless the prescribed fee is paid to the authority" without printing the numeric fee.

services.name: National Vehicle Number Plates & Registration (NVIS — 12 categories)
services.jurisdiction: Federal production (FRSC NVIS) & State BIR / MLA costing and collection
services.description: Production, registration, revalidation and verification of National Vehicle Number Plates across 12 private, commercial, motorcycle, articulated, out-of-series, fancy, dealer and government categories through the National Vehicle Identification Scheme (NVIS) and State Boards of Internal Revenue (SBIR).
requirements: Completed Form MVA 01 on https://nvis.frsc.gov.ng/ (30 mandatory fields: 17 vehicle description fields including chassis/VIN, engine number, make/model, colour and capacity, plus 13 owner identification and contact fields).
Custom duty papers / original purchase receipt / proof of ownership and valid identification (NIN / Driver's Licence / CAC documents for corporate bodies).
Police verification and physical vehicle inspection endorsement.
Costing assessment and payment confirmation by the State Board of Internal Revenue (SBIR) / Motor Licensing Authority (MLA).
processSteps: Initiate vehicle registration on https://nvis.frsc.gov.ng/VehicleManagement/RegisterVehicle (or revalidation at /VehicleManagement/Revalidation) to complete Form MVA 01, or obtain Form MVA 01 at the State Motor Licensing Authority (MLA).
Submit the form to the State Board of Internal Revenue (SBIR) / MLA for official costing and undergo Police verification and vehicle inspection.
Pay the assessed plate and registration charges into the designated State BIR / treasury bank account and obtain payment confirmation.
FRSC NVIS Desk Officer captures the verified vehicle and owner biometrics/data into the NVIS portal.
State BIR prints the Proof of Ownership Certificate (POC) and issues the physical National Vehicle Number Plate.
services.notes: Public NVIS portal: https://nvis.frsc.gov.ng/; Public FRSC Service Charter Appendix B (p. 20); SLA Printed pp. 11–12, PDF pp. 11–12. Multi-authority governance (FRSC / VIO / State IRS & JTB): FRSC designs and produces the National Driver's Licence and Number Plates and captures biometrics at Driver's Licence Centres (DLCs); State Vehicle Inspection Officers (VIO) conduct driver proficiency testing; State Boards of Internal Revenue (SBIR / FCT-IRS) and Motor Licensing Authorities (MLA / MVAA) determine state collectible charges through the Joint Tax Board (JTB), confirm payments and distribute permanent cards/plates. Because the public FRSC Service Charter PDF still lists legacy pre-revision plate rates (e.g. ₦12,500 standard motor vehicle, ₦2,500 motorcycle) while the restricted April 2026 SLA (p. 12) lists the revised 12-category JTB schedule (e.g. ₦30,000 standard motor vehicle, ₦12,000 motorcycle, ₦400,000 fancy) and notes that costing is done by State BIR, all 12 categories are preserved with their exact amounts and marked conflicting/pending state BIR confirmation.
services.paymentGuide: Start on https://nvis.frsc.gov.ng/ and complete costing and payment only through your State Board of Internal Revenue (SBIR) / Motor Licensing Authority (MLA). Note that State BIRs often bundle vehicle licence, roadworthiness, insurance and Proof of Ownership charges with the number plate fee.

services.name: Road Sign Production (FRSC Signage Plant, Gwagwalada)
services.jurisdiction: Federal (FRSC Headquarters Abuja & FRSC Signage Plant, Gwagwalada)
services.description: Custom production and supply of regulatory, warning and informational road traffic signs by the FRSC Signage Plant in Gwagwalada, Abuja for government agencies and private organisations.
requirements: Formal written application/order addressed to the Corps Marshal through the Deputy Corps Marshal, Motor Vehicle Administration — DCM (MVA) at FRSC National Headquarters, Abuja.
Exact technical specifications of the requested road signs: sign type, dimensions/sizes, reflectivity grade and quantity.
Remita payment receipt upon receiving the official FRSC costing assessment.
processSteps: Submit a formal road-sign production order to the Corps Marshal through DCM (MVA) specifying sign type, specification, sizes, grade and quantity.
DCM (MVA) acknowledges receipt of the order within 24 hours and forwards the specifications to the FRSC Signage Plant (Gwagwalada) for costing by the production officer.
Corps Commander (Signage) forwards the calculated production cost to the customer within 7 days.
Customer pays the assessed amount into the designated FRSC account via Remita and submits payment evidence to DCM (MVA).
FRSC Finance & Accounts Department confirms payment, after which DCM (MVA) communicates the delivery timeline, directs immediate production at the Signage Plant, and arranges dispatch.
services.notes: Public FRSC Services page (https://frsc.gov.ng/services) confirms the FRSC Signage Plant in Gwagwalada produces road signs; SLA Printed pp. 12–13, PDF pp. 12–13 details the 9-step order, 24-hour acknowledgement, 7-day costing and Remita payment workflow.
services.paymentGuide: Submit specifications to the Corps Marshal through DCM (MVA) at FRSC National Headquarters, wait for the official 7-day Signage Plant costing quotation, and pay only via Remita.

feeOptions.label: Custom road sign production quotation (by sign type, size, grade and quantity)
feeOptions.conditions: Bespoke quotation issued within 7 days of order acknowledgement (acknowledged within 24 hours). Paid via Remita before production commences.
feeOptions.notes: Variable by order specification; marked pending because the detailed 9-step costing workflow appears in the restricted SLA copy while the public FRSC services page provides only high-level plant information.
feeOptions.page: FRSC Services page; SLA Printed pp. 12–13, PDF pp. 12–13
feeOptions.evidenceNote: The FRSC Services page confirms the FRSC Signage Plant in Gwagwalada produces road signs; the April 2026 SLA (pp. 12–13) states that each order is costed individually by the Signage Plant production officer within 7 days based on sign type, specification, size and grade, and paid via Remita.

services.name: Vehicle Towing, Custody and Release of Towed Vehicles
services.jurisdiction: Federal highways & FRSC Field Commands nationwide
services.description: Towing of crashed, broken-down, obstructing or abandoned vehicles on highways, towing of non-crashed vehicles on owner request, and release of towed vehicles from FRSC custody.
requirements: For Towing on Request (non-crash vehicle, Public Towing SOP p. 5): Police report, vehicle papers certifying ownership, handwritten application, photocopy of valid ID (Driver's Licence, NIN or International Passport), completed Towing Requisition Form and Remita Retrieval Reference (RRR) payment receipt before towing.

For Claiming / Release of a Towed or Abandoned Vehicle (Public Towing SOP p. 6; SLA pp. 14, 16–17): Notice of Offence Sheet (where applicable), original Proof of Ownership (not handwritten) or court sworn affidavit, valid ID (Driver's Licence / Utility Bill / NIN), valid Vehicle Licence, two (2) passport-size photographs, and Remita receipts for tow charges, fines and any accrued custody fee.

Mandatory in-person verification at the FRSC Field Command: photograph of claimant standing beside the vehicle showing its registration number, MVA Central Databank verification, endorsement of the Vehicle Release Certificate (VRC) and issuance of a signed Gate Pass.
processSteps: Contact FRSC via the toll-free emergency line 122 or 0700-CALL-FRSC (070022553772), or report to the relevant FRSC Field Command Duty Room Officer (DRO).
Note: Under Public Towing SOP paragraph 10(c) (p. 5), a broken-down vehicle obstructing the highway with the owner in sight undergoing long repairs is towed off the road to a safe place at no cost.

For chargeable towing (FRSC-owned or PPP-coordinated tow trucks), generate a Remita Retrieval Reference (RRR) and pay the tow charge into CBN Account 0020104861033 ("FRSC Drivers Training, Towing Truck Donation and Others"), and pay any applicable traffic fine or daily custody fee (accruing after the initial 20 hours following arrest, SLA p. 14) into CBN Account 0020054141107 ("FRSC Consolidated Revenue Funds").
Present original payment receipts, proof of ownership, vehicle licence, ID and 2 passport photographs to the Duty Room Officer; take the mandatory verification photograph beside the vehicle.

Endorse the Vehicle Release Certificate (VRC), complete the Public Enlightenment Office (PEO) session where applicable, and present the signed Gate Pass at the Command gate to exit with the vehicle (Note: SLA p. 14 warns that impounded vehicles unclaimed after 6 months are subject to auction/forfeiture proceedings under Section 5(b) of the FRSC Act 2007).
services.notes: Public Towing SOP (22 October 2019, https://frsc.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/FINALa.pdf, pp. 1–8) and SLA Printed pp. 14–18; PDF pp. 14–18. Both sources state that FRSC tow charges are the average of prevailing commercial charges subject to distance, vehicle tonnage, terrain and PMS/AGO fuel price regime.
services.paymentGuide: Pay only via Remita into the designated CBN accounts listed in the FRSC Towing SOP and present the original receipt to the Field Command Duty Room Officer. Do not pay cash to patrol or tow-truck operatives.

feeOptions.label: Emergency roadside clearance of broken-down vehicle undergoing repairs with owner in sight (to a nearby safe place)
feeOptions.conditions: Applies only when a broken-down vehicle obstructing the highway is undergoing repairs with the owner in sight and the patrol team leader determines repairs will take a long time, towing it off the road to an immediate safe place.
feeOptions.notes: Substantiated directly by Paragraph 10(c) of the public 2019 FRSC Towing SOP.
feeOptions.page: Public Towing SOP (FINALa.pdf) Paragraph 10(c), PDF p. 5
feeOptions.evidenceNote: Paragraph 10(c) of the published FRSC Towing SOP (22 October 2019, p. 5) states: "Tow the vehicle off the road to a safe place at no cost if the repairs will take a long time."

feeOptions.label: Standard & on-request vehicle towing — 2019 SOP recommended guide (₦5,000–₦95,000) vs commercial-average formula
feeOptions.conditions: 2019 SOP recommended bands: <3 km (₦5,000–₦20,000), 3–5 km (₦10,000–₦40,000), 5–10 km (₦15,000–₦60,000), >10 km (₦25,000–₦80,000), 25–50 km (₦35,000–₦85,000), Night towing (₦40,000–₦95,000) across Cars/Light vs Heavy-Duty and Normal vs Difficult Terrain/Ditch. Subject to current PMS/AGO fuel regime and prevailing commercial rates.
feeOptions.notes: Marked conflicting because the public 2019 SOP prints the ₦5,000–₦95,000 recommended table while both the SOP and the 2026 SLA state that actual charges fluctuate with prevailing commercial rates and PMS/AGO fuel prices.
feeOptions.page: Public Towing SOP (FINALa.pdf) Paragraph 15, PDF p. 7; SLA Printed p. 17, PDF p. 17
feeOptions.evidenceNote: Paragraph 15 of the public 2019 Towing SOP (p. 7) states that tow charges are the average of prevailing commercial charges subject to distance, tonnage, terrain and PMS/AGO price regime, and publishes a recommended table from ₦5,000 (cars/light vehicles <3 km, normal terrain) up to ₦95,000 (heavy-duty vehicles in difficult terrain/ditch or night-time towing). The April 2026 SLA (p. 17) retains the variable commercial-average formula without re-publishing the 2019 numeric table.

feeOptions.label: Impounded / towed vehicle daily custody fee (after initial 20-hour grace period)
feeOptions.conditions: Accrues daily only after the initial 20 hours following vehicle arrest/impoundment; paid via Remita into FRSC Consolidated Revenue Funds.
feeOptions.notes: Daily naira rate is not stated in the SLA or public Towing SOP; recorded as pending/unknown.
feeOptions.page: Public Towing SOP (FINALa.pdf) Paragraph 11(b), PDF p. 6; SLA Printed p. 14, PDF p. 14
feeOptions.evidenceNote: Both the public 2019 Towing SOP (p. 6, Paragraph 11b) and the April 2026 SLA (p. 14, Note iii) state that a Custody Fee is payable into the FRSC Consolidated Revenue Fund (CBN Account 0020054141107) and accrues daily after the initial 20 hours following arrest, but neither document states the numeric daily custody rate.

services.name: Speed Limiting Device (SLD) Vendor Accreditation
services.jurisdiction: Federal (FRSC National Headquarters Abuja, SON & NADDC)
services.description: Corporate accreditation and biannual inspection of vendors authorised to supply, install, calibrate and maintain Speed Limiting Devices (SLDs) in motor vehicles in Nigeria.
requirements: 1. Certificate of Incorporation with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC).
2. Comprehensive Company Profile.
3. Evidence of filing of Annual Returns to CAC for the last 3 years.
4. Curriculum Vitae (CV) of key technical personnel.
5. Current Tax Clearance Certificate (TCC) for the last 3 years.
6. Value Added Tax (VAT) Registration Certificate.
7. Audited Accounts of the company for the last 3 years.
8. Reference letter from a reputable bank.
9. Verifiable list of at least 3 similar projects successfully executed by the company.
10. Evidence of compliance with the Industrial Training Fund (ITF).
11. Evidence of compliance with the Pension Reform Act (PENCOM).
12. Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) Speed Limiting Device Product Certificate.
processSteps: Submit a formal application with all 12 pre-qualification documents to the Corps Marshal at FRSC National Headquarters, Abuja.

Undergo document screening and technical evaluation by the Inter-Agency Technical Committee comprising FRSC, Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) and National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC); minimum cut-off score is 60% (notified within 2 weeks).
Undergo physical inspection of the vendor's Fitness/Installation Centre(s) across the federation within 6 weeks.
Successful vendors receive their FRSC Accreditation Certificate within 2 weeks after inspection approval and are onboarded to the FRSC Speed Limiting Device portal.
Submit to mandatory biannual (twice-yearly) post-accreditation inspection by the Technical Committee.
services.notes: Public FRSC Services page (https://frsc.gov.ng/services) confirms the Speed Limiting Device programme; SLA Printed pp. 18–20, PDF pp. 18–20 details the 12 pre-qualification requirements, 60% Technical Committee threshold, 2-week screening notification, 6-week facility inspection, 2-week certificate presentation and biannual re-inspection.
services.paymentGuide: Submit pre-qualification documents to the Corps Marshal at FRSC National Headquarters, Abuja and confirm any applicable accreditation or inspection fee directly with FRSC.

feeOptions.label: Speed Limiting Device (SLD) vendor accreditation fee
feeOptions.conditions: Corporate vendor accreditation subject to 12 pre-qualification documents, 60% FRSC/SON/NADDC Technical Committee evaluation score and physical fitness-centre inspection.
feeOptions.notes: No fee is stated in the SLA or public FRSC pages; recorded as pending/unknown, never assumed free.
feeOptions.page: FRSC Services page; SLA Printed pp. 18–20, PDF pp. 18–20
feeOptions.evidenceNote: Neither the public FRSC Services page nor the April 2026 SLA (pp. 18–20) states a fee amount for Speed Limiting Device vendor accreditation.
